title: Adaptive commit phasing and ephemeral slots PRD (WIP)
body:
Purpose:
This doc sketches a new approach for Dedicated capacity that smooths customer commit shocks and enables short-lived ephemeral capacity to absorb spikes with predictable isolation and cost behavior. Idea is to separate long-lived committed slots from short-lived ephemeral slots and introduce a commit-phasing controller plus a stochastic smoothing ledger so we can guarantee tenant isolation while giving flexible burst capacity.

Context / problem:
- Customers want the predictability of reserved capacity but also need cheap transient headroom for unpredictable spikes (batch prep, promotions, flash usage).
- Existing designs either over-provision (expensive) or allow noisy neighbors during bursts.
- Need better SLO-aligned degradation: preserve critical low-latency lanes while allowing best-effort workloads to be time-shifted or throttled.

Principles:
- Two pools: committed (hard-guarantee, long-lived) and ephemeral (soft-guarantee, short-lived).
- Commit-phasing: new capacity commitments migrate from tentative -> warming -> active over a configurable window to avoid sudden capacity jumps that break placement and billing.
- Ephemeral slots: tiny, short TTL allocations that can be preempted with predictable credit accounting.
- Smoothing ledger: each tenant has a credit balance that accrues slowly (commit amortization) and is spent on ephemeral use; ledger behavior governed by stochastic dampening parameters.

High-level proposal:
1) Commitment lifecycle: request commit -> phasing window (default 24h) -> active. During phasing we reserve minimal placement slack and pre-warm models; billing starts at commit request but at discounted pro-rated rate until active. This reduces churn and avoids instantaneous rebalancing.
2) Ephemeral allocator: allocate ephemeral slots from a shared ephemeral pool up to per-tenant credit limit; ephemeral TTL default 10 minutes; can be extended if credits available; preemption order: ephemeral -> burst-lane best-effort -> background.
3) Credit ledger: tenants earn credits based on long-lived commit size and time (e.g., 0.2 credits per vGPU-hour committed per day). Credits cap at configurable multiple of commit size. Spend on ephemeral allocations or priority lanes. Credits decay if unused to avoid unlimited bank.
4) Isolation controls: when capacity contention occurs, system enforces: a) protect critical routes (customer-defined tag) b) throttle or evict ephemeral usage beyond credit threshold c) fall back to smaller model variants for low-priority routes.

Autoscaling behavior:
- Autoscaler considers committed headroom separately from ephemeral demand forecasts.
- For committed autoscale: require sustained signal over commit-phasing window before adding new committed nodes to avoid oscillation.
- For ephemeral autoscale: scale ephemeral pool opportunistically based on spare cluster capacity, with explicit circuit-breaker when cross-tenant isolation risk is high.

Operational considerations:
- Metrics: credit_balance, ephemeral_alloc_rate, ephemeral_evictions, commit_phase_backlog, commit_warm_success_rate, tenant_isolation_incidents.
- Cost accounting: ephemeral usage billed at higher per-minute rate, tied to credit consumption; clear per-route token-level breakdown in Console.
- Rollout plan: start with opt-in for a subset of engineering accounts -> internal soak -> beta customers -> gradual public release.

User stories:
- As a platform engineer I want short-lived slots for nightly batch bursts without buying more reserved capacity.
- As an enterprise customer I want guarantees that my low-latency endpoints are not preempted by other tenants' ephemeral spikes.
- As an SRE I want visibility into which tenants are consuming ephemeral credits so I can tune policies.

Tradeoffs / open questions:
- Pricing model: flat premium for ephemeral minutes vs credit-backed discounted model. Need finance sanity check.
- Phasing window length: short windows reduce friction but increase placement churn. Trade-off experiments needed.
- Credit accrual formula: linear vs diminishing returns; how to prevent gaming.
- Ephemeral pool sizing: risk of overcommitting shared ephemeral pool and creating noisy neighbor issues.

Next steps / immediate tasks:
- Simulation: run 14-day traffic replay across representative tenant mix to model credit ledger behavior and eviction rates (owner: Leo).
- Prototype: implement phase controller in dev cluster with commit tagging and soft pre-warm (owner: Ava).
- Billing design sync with finance (owner: Riya).
- Console changes: surface credit balance and ephemeral allocations per-tenant (owner: Noah).

Notes / adhoc thoughts:
- Could pair ephemeral slots with lightweight quantized model variants to reduce per-slot cost and make preemption cheaper.
- Consider offering 'burst insurance' where customers buy short-term pre-warmed lanes for predictable events.
- Put a hard cap on ephemeral spend per-account and alert customers via email/SMS if approaching cap.
